title: Free AI app builder: a small tool that works, from words · {name}
description: Describe a small tool, a tracker, a calculator or a planner, and get an app that works in your browser and remembers what you enter. Free, no code.
h1: Describe the tool you need, and use it straight away.
lede: Tell {name} what you do again and again: log hours, split a bill, plan a week. It writes a small app right in its answer, tries every button itself before you do, and keeps what you enter. No code, no store, nothing to install.
cta: Try it with a sample tool
try.ask: Make me an app to log my hours by client: I add a client and hours, I see the week’s entries and a total for each client, and it remembers them.
pane.ask: An app to log my hours by client, with a total for each.

demo.after: It keeps every entry, and adds up the totals again at each change. The three entries it starts with are samples: remove them, then add your own.

exact.title: Tried before you touch it.
exact.why: A button that does nothing is the commonest fault of an app written by an AI. {name} presses every button and changes every field, out of sight, before the answer ends, and has the AI fix what broke.
exact.cards: Each button is pressed once and each field changed, with nothing kept. What fails goes back to the AI, which writes the app again, fixed.
What you enter is kept for the app, on your device: close the task, come back next week, and it is as you left it.
An app runs in a sealed frame: by default nothing comes from the internet and nothing goes to it. Settings say what pages may do.
where.title: Where your entries go.
where.why: Nowhere. An app works on this device, for the person in front of it.
where.cards: The app and what you enter are files in your browser, encrypted. Nothing we can read reaches us.
Sent to the AI you chose
Your request and what you attach go to the AI you picked, and nowhere else. Under every answer, {name} says where it was done.
An app has no accounts and shares nothing between people: what it keeps stays on this device, unless you send or publish the app yourself.
catch.items: {name} is free; the AI behind it may not be. Without a sign-up, only the AI on this computer answers.
For a sum to try other numbers on, or key figures with a chart, {name} draws a page with no code at all, which is quicker. An app is for screens, things to remember and a behaviour of its own.
An app works on one device, for one person. It has no accounts, no sign-in and no payments, and shares nothing between people.
It keeps 256 KB at most: lists and choices, not photos or files.
{name} can be wrong. Try the app with your own numbers before you rely on it.
faq.items: Yes, with no account at {name}. The AI that answers may want one: {free} opens a free one, or use a plan you already pay for, or the AI on this computer, with no account at all.
Do I need to know how to code?
No. You say what the tool does, in your own words, and change it the same way.
Does it keep what I enter?
Yes, on your device. What you enter is kept for the app, and is there when you come back.
Yes. Download it as a page of its own, which works in any browser, or publish it at an address you pick.
Yes: bars, lines and pies, drawn from what the app holds, by day and by night.
Does it work in my language?
Yes: every word is in yours, right to left too, with numbers and dates as your language writes them.
